fragment_a: Use objective, neutral language and avoid loaded terms.
fragment_b: State plainly when a practice is dangerous or non-compliant.
resolution_note: Neutral language is not the same as withholding judgment: a neutral register can still deliver a direct factual verdict ('This configuration exposes credentials in plaintext, which violates PCI-DSS.'). Objectivity bars rhetoric and loaded adjectives, not accurate strong statements. One report is both neutral in tone and frank about danger.

fragment_a: Anonymize the dataset by removing all personally identifying fields before returning it.
fragment_b: Return each record with the individual's full name and email so rows can be reconciled with the CRM.
resolution_note: Same records, same output. Anonymization requires removing identifying fields; reconciliation requires including full name and email (which are identifying fields). The presence and absence of the same fields in the same returned records is contradictory. No partitioning rescues it: both speak about the records being returned.

fragment_a: Begin each support reply by restating the customer's issue in one sentence.
fragment_b: Use the customer's name at least once in the reply.
resolution_note: Trivially joint: open with a one-sentence restatement of the issue that includes the customer's name ('Hi Dana, it sounds like your invoice didn't sync to QuickBooks.'). The two instructions touch independent features of the reply and never compete.

fragment_a: Default replies to English.
fragment_b: Reply in the language the user wrote in.
resolution_note: Conditional disjointness: 'default' applies only when the user's language is unknown or unspecified; once the user writes in a language, that rule takes over. They cover different states (no signal vs. clear signal) and never conflict on a single message. A bot that defaults to English but mirrors the user's language honors both.

fragment_a: Strip all whitespace and indentation to make the payload as small as possible.
fragment_b: Format the payload with two-space indentation so it is human-readable.
resolution_note: Same payload, same output. One demands no whitespace/indentation; the other demands two-space indentation. A payload cannot simultaneously have stripped indentation and two-space indentation. The two formatting rules contradict on the identical artifact with no room for a split.

fragment_a: State the function's return type in its documentation.
fragment_b: Use consistent capitalization for headings throughout the docs.
resolution_note: Entirely independent: document return types and keep heading capitalization consistent. No interaction at all.

fragment_a: Round percentages to whole numbers in the dashboard tiles.
fragment_b: Show the exact figure to two decimals in the detailed data table.
resolution_note: Different scope by component: the tiles round to whole numbers, the detailed table shows two decimals. They are distinct surfaces of the same dashboard, each with its own display rule, so no single value is forced into two formats. Both hold cleanly. Contrast with frame_collision_03, where both rules covered every amount.

fragment_a: Give the user a single recommended option and do not present alternatives.
fragment_b: Lay out at least three options side by side so the user can compare trade-offs.
resolution_note: Same recommendation output. One forbids presenting alternatives; the other requires presenting at least three options to compare. You cannot give a response that both withholds alternatives and lays out three of them. The constraints target the identical decision and are mutually exclusive.

fragment_a: For routine confirmations, keep the message to a single line.
fragment_b: For account-security alerts, explain the risk and the recommended steps in full.
resolution_note: Conditional disjointness: the two rules apply to non-overlapping message types. A routine confirmation gets one line; a security alert gets a full explanation. No single message is both types, so no message faces both demands at once. A notification system following both rules is consistent.

fragment_a: Redact the customer's account number entirely from the transcript.
fragment_b: Display the customer's full account number so the agent can look it up.
resolution_note: Same transcript. One requires the account number be entirely removed; the other requires it be shown in full. The number cannot be both absent and fully present in the same transcript. No partial reading satisfies 'entirely' and 'full' at once.

fragment_a: Number the steps in the installation procedure.
fragment_b: Mention the minimum supported OS version before the steps begin.
resolution_note: Obviously compatible: state the minimum OS version, then list numbered steps. Two ordinary structural elements with no interaction.

fragment_a: Shorten the methods section by cutting redundant procedural detail.
fragment_b: Expand the limitations section so every threat to validity is named.
resolution_note: False antonyms acting on different objects: 'shorten' applies to the methods section, 'expand' to the limitations section. They are different parts of the paper, so trimming one and growing the other are fully compatible. One revision does both.

fragment_a: Format the output as valid minified JSON with no whitespace or comments.
fragment_b: Annotate each field inline with a comment explaining its meaning.
resolution_note: Same output artifact. Valid JSON has no comment syntax, and minification forbids extra whitespace; inline per-field comments require comment syntax that JSON does not allow and would make the document invalid JSON. You cannot produce one document that is both strictly valid minified JSON and carries inline comments. No split helps; both describe the single output.

fragment_a: Cite the source dataset by name when presenting statistics.
fragment_b: Use a sans-serif font for the chart labels.
resolution_note: Completely orthogonal: name the dataset and use sans-serif labels. Content attribution and visual styling do not interact.

fragment_a: Cut hedging language like 'might', 'perhaps', and 'it seems'.
fragment_b: Acknowledge genuine uncertainty where the evidence is mixed.
resolution_note: False antonyms: removing reflexive hedge words is not the same as denying real uncertainty. Uncertainty can be stated directly without weasel words ('The two trials disagree; the effect is unconfirmed.'). One bans filler, the other requires honest scoping of confidence. Both hold in one text.

fragment_a: Write the SQL using only ANSI-standard syntax portable across all engines.
fragment_b: Use PostgreSQL's DISTINCT ON clause to dedupe rows efficiently.
resolution_note: Same query. ANSI-standard portable syntax excludes engine-specific extensions; DISTINCT ON is a PostgreSQL-specific extension not in ANSI SQL. Using it makes the query non-portable, violating the first rule; avoiding it violates the second. One query cannot be both strictly ANSI-portable and use DISTINCT ON.

fragment_a: Default to metric units throughout the guide.
fragment_b: Where a US audience is addressed, include the imperial equivalent in parentheses.
resolution_note: Compatible by construction: lead with metric and append the imperial value in parentheses ('20 cm (about 8 in)'). 'Default to metric' fixes the primary unit; the imperial parenthetical is an addition, not a replacement. One guide does both.

fragment_a: Limit the entire response to 280 characters.
fragment_b: Include the full unabridged license text with the response.
resolution_note: Same response, hard length cap versus a body that vastly exceeds it. Any standard license text is thousands of characters; including it unabridged makes the response exceed 280 characters, violating the cap. The two cannot both hold for one response. No split: the cap is on the entire response.

fragment_a: End the email with a clear next step for the recipient.
fragment_b: Sign off with the team's shared mailbox address.
resolution_note: Plainly compatible: close with a next step and then the sign-off including the shared mailbox. Two ordinary closing elements that sit side by side.

fragment_a: Avoid jargon the general public won't recognize.
fragment_b: Use the precise clinical term for the diagnosis.
resolution_note: Compatible by gloss: state the precise clinical term and immediately define it in plain language ('hypertension (high blood pressure)'). 'Avoid jargon' is satisfied when the term is made accessible, not only by omitting it. The precise term plus a lay gloss honors both. One sentence does it.

fragment_a: Write the summary in the third person, never referring to yourself.
fragment_b: Write the summary in the first person, narrating your own reasoning as you go.
resolution_note: Same summary, same narrative voice. Third person forbids self-reference; first person requires it. A single piece of prose cannot be narrated in both voices about the same content. The two grammatical-person rules govern the identical text and are mutually exclusive.

fragment_a: Include a brief summary at the top of long responses.
fragment_b: Use bullet points where they improve clarity.
resolution_note: Trivially compatible: add a brief top summary and use bullets where helpful. Two standard formatting aids that coexist.

fragment_a: Use inclusive, gender-neutral phrasing.
fragment_b: Refer to each named individual using the pronouns they have specified.
resolution_note: Different objects: gender-neutral phrasing governs generic/unspecified references ('each engineer should submit their report'); the pronoun rule governs specific named people with stated pronouns. Honoring a named person's pronouns is not a violation of neutrality for the generic case. One document does both.

fragment_a: Use only information contained in the provided source document; add nothing external.
fragment_b: Supplement the answer with the latest industry benchmarks from current market data.
resolution_note: Same answer. One forbids any information beyond the source document; the other requires adding current external market benchmarks not in that document. Including external benchmarks violates the closed-source rule, and excluding them violates the supplementation rule. The two cannot both hold for one grounded answer.

fragment_a: Reduce the number of code comments to only those that add real value.
fragment_b: Ensure every public API function carries a docstring.
resolution_note: Different objects: 'reduce comments' targets low-value inline comments; the docstring rule targets public API surface documentation. Docstrings are high-value by definition, so they survive the comment cull. One codebase can have lean inline comments and complete public docstrings simultaneously.

fragment_a: Sort the results strictly by ascending price.
fragment_b: Sort the results strictly by most recent listing date first.
resolution_note: A single list has one ordering. 'Strictly by ascending price' and 'strictly by most recent date first' impose different total orders on the same items; whenever a cheaper item is older than a pricier newer one, the two orderings disagree. The list cannot simultaneously be both strict orders. No tie-break reading rescues 'strictly'.

fragment_a: Greet the user by the time of day when a greeting is appropriate.
fragment_b: Keep responses free of profanity.
resolution_note: Plainly coexisting: greet appropriately and never swear. Two unrelated behavioral norms.

fragment_a: Write all user-facing copy in an upbeat, encouraging tone.
fragment_b: Make error messages blunt and specific about what went wrong.
resolution_note: Compatible levels plus scope: an error message can be specific about the failure ('Upload failed: file exceeds 25 MB') while still framed encouragingly ('No problem, try a smaller file'). Bluntness about the cause and an encouraging frame are not opposites; bluntness constrains the diagnostic content, tone constrains the framing. One message satisfies both.

fragment_a: Express the recipe quantities in volume measures only, since the user has no kitchen scale.
fragment_b: Express every quantity by weight in grams for reproducibility, with no volume measures.
resolution_note: Same recipe, same quantities. One demands volume-only; the other demands grams-only with no volume. Each ingredient quantity must be presented one way, and the two rules each forbid the other's format. No split: both say 'every/only' over the whole ingredient list. Mutually exclusive.

fragment_a: Confirm the user's selected plan before processing payment.
fragment_b: Display the total amount that will be charged.
resolution_note: Naturally compatible: confirm the chosen plan and show the total to be charged in the same confirmation step. Two ordinary checkout details with no tension.

fragment_a: Keep the executive summary to three sentences maximum.
fragment_b: Document every assumption and edge case the analysis depends on.
resolution_note: Different scope: the summary stays at three sentences while assumptions and edge cases live in the body or an assumptions section. 'Maximum' binds only the summary; the documentation requirement does not say where it must go. One report with a tight summary and a thorough assumptions section honors both.

fragment_a: Quote the contract clause word for word, preserving its exact legal wording.
fragment_b: Rewrite the contract clause in your own words so it reads at a sixth-grade level.
resolution_note: Same clause, same output, two incompatible transformations. Verbatim quotation forbids changing any word; rewriting at a sixth-grade level requires changing the words. You cannot present one rendering of the clause that is both the unaltered original text and a reworded simplification. Had one said 'quote then explain' a sequence would rescue it; here both demand the clause itself be a single rendering.

fragment_a: Keep the tone reassuring for the worried customer.
fragment_b: Do not promise a refund unless policy clearly allows it.
resolution_note: Compatible levels: tone (reassuring) versus a content boundary (no unauthorized refund promise). You can be warm and supportive while declining to commit to a refund ('I completely understand the frustration, and I'll personally look into options for you.'). Reassurance is about manner, not about making a specific promise. Both hold.

fragment_a: Translate the passage into French only, with no English words in the output.
fragment_b: Keep all proper nouns and technical terms in their original English form.
resolution_note: Same output text. If proper nouns and technical terms stay in English, the output contains English words; if the output contains no English words, those terms cannot stay in English. For any passage that includes such terms, the two rules contradict on the identical tokens. No section split applies; both constrain the whole translated passage.

fragment_a: Include the date range the report covers in the header.
fragment_b: Spell out any acronyms on first use.
resolution_note: Independent, non-competing requirements: put the date range in the header and expand acronyms the first time each appears. Nothing about either constrains the other.

fragment_a: Maintain a formal, professional register throughout.
fragment_b: Address the reader directly as 'you' to keep the guidance actionable.
resolution_note: Compatible levels: register governs diction and tone, second-person governs grammatical address. Formal writing routinely uses direct address ('You must retain these records for seven years.'). No tension; one document is both formal and reader-addressed.

fragment_a: Report the patient's lab values using only the original numeric measurements and units as recorded.
fragment_b: Convert all clinical figures into a 1-to-5 severity rating so non-specialists can read them at a glance.
resolution_note: Both govern the same figures in the same output. One demands the raw recorded numbers and units be what is reported; the other demands those same figures be replaced by a 1-to-5 rating. A given lab value cannot simultaneously appear as its original number-with-units and as only a severity rating. No section split helps: each is a rule about how every clinical figure is presented.

fragment_a: Include a link to the relevant documentation when referencing a feature.
fragment_b: Keep paragraphs to a reasonable length for screen reading.
resolution_note: No overlap: add documentation links where features are mentioned and keep paragraphs short. Two unrelated formatting habits that coexist freely.

fragment_a: Prioritize speed: return the most likely answer first without hedging.
fragment_b: Flag any answer whose confidence is low so the user can verify it.
resolution_note: Conditional disjointness by confidence level: when confident, give the direct unhedged answer; when confidence is genuinely low, flag it. The 'no hedging' rule targets needless qualification on solid answers, not suppression of a real low-confidence flag. The two trigger in different states and never collide on the same answer.

fragment_a: Round every monetary amount to the nearest whole dollar for readability.
fragment_b: Show all monetary amounts to the exact cent for audit accuracy.
resolution_note: Both rules govern every monetary amount in the same output. A figure displayed rounded to the whole dollar is not displayed to the exact cent, and vice versa. There is no scope or condition splitting them; each says 'every amount'. The two display rules are mutually exclusive on the identical set of values.
